To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of the OpenEdition.org platform is a very interesting source for the automatic collection of scholarly book reviews and the supervised classification of the reviews into two classes (book reviews and non-book reviews) can be achieved with an accuracy of 90% using the SVM approach.
the best results are achieved with a SVM classifier and a combination of the following features: the title and the content of the document and the number of words in the document.

1) the use of a combination of features, including both textual and non-textual features, is more effective than the use of a single type of features; 2) the combination of textual features and non-textual ones is more efficient than the use of only one of them; and 3) the use of textual features is better than the use of non-textual ones.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approaches are able to classify scholarly book reviews with an accuracy of 80.7%, which is a very good result.
the best performance is obtained by the SVM classifier with the TF-IDF representation.
our approach can be considered as a first step towards the automatic identification and classification of scholarly book reviews.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best results are obtained by combining the different document representations and by using a simple SVM classifier.
the best results for the classification of scholarly book reviews are obtained with a combination of two different features: a bag-of-words and a bag-of-concepts.
we have shown that it is possible to collect and classify the scholarly book reviews from OpenEdition platform and Web with high precision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to collect reviews from different sources, to build a corpus of scholarly book reviews and to use it for the automatic linking of the reviews to the corresponding book in the future.
the automatic classification is not an easy task, and that the best results are obtained by combining different approaches and features.
the use of different representations of documents can improve the classification performance and thus, the automatic links.
